Socrates, a classical Greek philosopher, employed several methods to challenge the prevailing thoughts of his time. Some of the methods he used include:

1. Dialogue: Socrates engaged in many dialogues with his fellow citizens, during which he would ask the participants questions and encourage them to think critically about the issues at hand. He would use his mastery of the art of logical reasoning to expose the flaws in their arguments.

2. Logic: Socrates was a master of logic and used it to systematically unravel the inconsistencies in people's beliefs and arguments. He would often use the famous Socratic Method, which involved asking a series of questions that would lead the person to evaluate their own arguments and assumptions.

3. Induction: Socrates believed that the best way to learn about the world around us was to draw conclusions based on what we can observe and experience. This meant that he also employed methods of induction to challenge the prevailing thoughts of his time, such as the myths and legends that were commonly believed.

4. Questioning Authority: Socrates was not afraid to challenge the prevailing thought of his time, even if it meant going against the authority of the established leaders in the city. He believed that it was important to question everything, even the most sacred of traditions.

In summary, Socrates used several methods, such as Dialogue, Logic, Induction, and Questioning Authority, to challenge the prevailing thoughts of his time.</s>
